questions.question: Ryotwari system of revenue collection in India, introduced by the British, was based on the _______.
questions.solution:
• Economic Theory: Ricardian theory of rent
  • Fact: The Ryotwari System was based on David Ricardo's theory, where rent is paid for the original and indestructible powers of the soil.

questions.question: In Chola administration, ________ was the assembly in the villages which were inhabited predominantly by the Brahmanas.
questions.solution:
• Chola Admin: Sabha
  • Context: The Sabha was an assembly of Brahmin landholders, while the Ur was the assembly of common villages.

questions.question: Who among the following was the founder of ‘Tiger Legion' or ‘Free India Legion'?
questions.solution:
• Founder: Subhas Chandra Bose
  • Detail: The Tiger Legion (Free India Legion) was a military unit raised in Germany to fight for Indian independence.

questions.question: The Vedic Aryans lived in the area called Sapt-Sindhu, which means area drained by seven rivers. One of the rivers among the seven is Jhelum. What was its ancient name?
questions.solution:
• River Name: Vitasta
  • Vedic Geography: The Jhelum was known as Vitasta; other names include Asikni (Chenab) and Parushni (Ravi).

questions.question: Who among the following was the author of the play ‘Mrichchhakatika’?
questions.solution:
• Literature: Shudraka
  • Work: Mrichchhakatika (The Little Clay Cart) is a Sanskrit play set in the city of Ujjain.

questions.question: Who among the following was defeated in the battle of Chanderi in 1528?
questions.solution:
• Battle: Medini Rai
  • History: In the Battle of Chanderi (1528), Babur defeated the Rajput leader Medini Rai.

questions.question: Before the rise of the modern industrial system, Indian exports consisted chiefly of manufactures like________.
questions.solution:
• Indian Exports: cotton and silk fabrics
  • Fact: Before the British industrial system, India was the world leader in exporting high-quality handloom textiles.

questions.question: Pathans in North-West India organised the society of Khudai Khidmatgars, popularly known as Red Shirt, under whose leadership?
questions.solution:
• Leader: Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan
  • Movement: Known as the 'Frontier Gandhi,' he led the Khudai Khidmatgars (Red Shirts) in the North-West.

questions.question: Which of the following was established in Bombay in 1875?
questions.solution:
• Organization: Arya Samaj
  • Establishment: Founded by Swami Dayanand Saraswati in Bombay in 1875 to promote Vedic values.

questions.question: The Shailendra kings who founded their empire in South-east Asia in the 8th Century AD were the followers of _________.
questions.solution:
• Religion: Buddhism
  • Empire: The Shailendra kings of South-east Asia were great patrons of Mahayana Buddhism and built Borobudur.

questions.question: A wealthy person in the early Vedic period was known as ______.
questions.solution:
• Term: Gomat
  • Vedic Society: A wealthy person was called Gomat because wealth was measured by the ownership of cows.

questions.question: ________ announced the bifurcation of the British Indian Empire into a secular India and Islamic Pakistan.
questions.solution:
• Viceroy: Lord Louis Mountbatten
  • Event: He announced the 3rd June Plan which led to the partition of India and Pakistan.

questions.question: Who among the following was the first person to discuss poverty line in pre-independent India?
questions.solution:
• Poverty Line: Dadabhai Naoroji
  • Contribution: In his work 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India', he was the first to calculate a subsistence cost as a poverty line.

questions.question: Vijayanagara emperor Krishnadeva Raya founded a suburban township near Vijayanagara called Nagalapuram after his ________.
questions.solution:
• Township: mother
  • Vijayanagara: Krishnadeva Raya founded Nagalapuram in memory of his mother, Nagala Devi.

questions.question: Under whom was CP Ilbert a law member of the council?
questions.solution:
• Viceroy: Lord Ripon
  • Fact: CP Ilbert introduced the Ilbert Bill under Ripon, which sought to allow Indian judges to try Europeans.

questions.question: Which Chinese traveller visited India during the reign of Harshavardhana?
questions.solution:
• Traveler: Hsuan Tsang
  • Context: Also known as Xuanzang, he stayed in India for 15 years during Harshavardhana's reign.

questions.question: Who was the first social reformer to view modern education as a vehicle for the spread of modern ideas in the country?
questions.solution:
• Reformer: Raja Ram Mohan Roy
  • Idea: He advocated for Western education and science to modernize Indian society.

questions.question: Which of the following organisations is credited with writing literary pieces for the abolition of Sati Pratha?
questions.solution:
• Organization: The Brahmo Samaj
  • Social Reform: This group was instrumental in the 1829 legislation that abolished Sati.

questions.question: Name the French jeweller who travelled to India at least six times during the Mughal period.
questions.solution:
• Traveler: Jean-Baptiste Tavernier
  • Detail: A French gem merchant who provided detailed accounts of the Peacock Throne and the Koh-i-Noor diamond.

questions.question: Which of the following reforming societies believed Vedas to be the fountain of all the knowledge?
questions.solution:
• Society: Arya Samaj
  • Belief: Their primary slogan was 'Go Back to the Vedas' as they considered them the source of all truth.

questions.question: Which of the following systems of the Delhi sultanate had a influence on the Bahmani and Vijayanagar kingdoms?
questions.solution:
• System: Iqtadari
  • Legacy: The Iqta system of the Delhi Sultanate (land grants for military service) was adapted into the Nayankara system in Vijayanagar.

questions.question: What was the function of an officer called Samaharta?
questions.solution:
• Officer: Samaharta
  • Mauryan Admin: The Samaharta was the Chief Collector of Revenue; the Sannidhata was the Treasurer.

questions.question: Who led the English army in the Battle of Buxar?
questions.solution:
• Commander: Hector Munro
  • Battle: He led the British to victory in the Battle of Buxar (1764) against the combined forces of Mir Qasim.

questions.question: Who is the author of Tarikh-i-Firuz Shahi?
questions.solution:
• Author: Ziauddin Barani
  • Work: Tarikh-i-Firuz Shahi is a major source for the history of the Tughlaq and Khilji dynasties.

questions.question: During the reign of which of the following rulers did Hiuen Tsang, a Chinese traveller, come to India?
questions.solution:
• Visit: Harshavardhana
  • Traveler: The Chinese pilgrim Hiuen Tsang visited the court of Harsha and the university at Nalanda.

questions.question: Sohan Singh Bhakna and Har Dayal were primarily associated with which of the following organisations?
questions.solution:
• Party: Ghadar Party
  • Founders: Established in San Francisco to overthrow British rule via armed revolution.

questions.question: Who was the founder of Harijan Sevak Sangh founded in 1932?
questions.solution:
• Founder: Mahatma Gandhi
  • Organization: Harijan Sevak Sangh was formed after the Poona Pact to work for the upliftment of Depressed Classes.

questions.question: Who was behind publishing the first News Paper in India?
questions.solution:
• Newspaper: James Augustus Hickey
  • First: He started the Bengal Gazette in 1780, the first printed newspaper in India.

questions.question: Nana Sahib, a rebel at Kanpur was the son of which of the following Peshwas?
questions.solution:
• Rebel: Baji Rao II
  • 1857: Nana Sahib was the adopted son of the last Peshwa, Baji Rao II, and led the revolt in Kanpur.

questions.question: Ashoka sent a mission to spread the principle of Dhamma led by his son, Mahendra and daughter, Sanghamitra to _______.
questions.solution:
• Mission: Ceylon
  • Spread of Dhamma: Ashoka's children converted the king of Ceylon (Sri Lanka) to Buddhism.
